title: Avoid false positives when safety checks match approved voice
description:
## Dogfood reproduction

After the document-output truncation fix, a live suggestion for `https://anth.us/blog/commodity-receipts/` was rejected by `suggestions_contain_evasion_tactics`. The source article itself contains `ngl`; the current detector treats any occurrence of `ngl` anywhere in a complete candidate as detector-evasion, even if the model is preserving approved source voice.

## Intent

As a caller requesting safe editorial suggestions, I want Limatus to block actual detector-evasion instructions without rejecting legitimate source or house-voice language, so safety policy does not erase the editorial register it is meant to protect.

## Gherkin

Feature: Contextual detector-evasion safety checks
  Scenario: Preserve approved colloquial source language
    Given a source draft that uses an ordinary colloquial term such as `ngl`
    When Limatus returns a suggestion that preserves the term without instructing evasion
    Then the suggestion is accepted for review

  Scenario: Reject an evasion instruction
    Given a suggestion that recommends adding slang or fake experience to evade detection
    When Limatus validates it
    Then it rejects the suggestion with a safety error

## Scope

Make the safety policy contextual: distinguish meta-instructions/reasons that prescribe evasion from candidate prose that legitimately contains a term. Test both paths offline.

## Out of scope

Removing safety guardrails, allowing detector-score optimization, or changing the caller editorial workflow.
